I have $889 and own Atlantic Avenue, which is yellow. The auction high bid is $112 by p1. I am deciding whether to bid $113 or drop out.

I need to keep enough cash to survive New York or Virginia. Dark blue properties will stay unbuilt until my cushion is safe.

Bidding $113 is still below the $140 mortgage floor, so I can flip the property for net cash and complete the yellow set.

p1 has $320 cash but is in jail with an orange monopoly and mortgaged red properties. He is bidding one dollar higher each turn.

p1 may be chasing the same mortgage arbitrage or trying to block the yellow set. I am weighing whether the property is worth more than its $140 mortgage value to me. p4 owns Ventnor but is cash-poor with hotels and railroads.

I am weighing whether to keep one-dollar increments or jump the bid to end the auction faster. A large jump might signal strong interest and push p1 higher, or it could end the auction if I bid past his cash limit. p1 has no yellow properties and would treat the property as a mortgage flip worth roughly $140.

p1 may bid above $140 to block me from completing the yellow set. He has $320 cash but is in jail with an orange monopoly already built, so he cannot collect rent immediately. Blocking me would cost him roughly $30 extra for a property worth only $140. Without Ventnor, a yellow monopoly is incomplete and offers little strategic value.

I will bid $113 and keep one-dollar increments until the bid nears $140. I am checking orange house rent values to confirm my cash cushion can cover New York Avenue.
